replies.send: what's the difference between a Chianti Classico and a Riserva?
replies.reply:
Great question! Here's the breakdown:

*Chianti Classico*
The standard tier — made from at least 80% Sangiovese grapes grown in the Classico zone (between Florence and Siena). Aged a minimum of 12 months before release. Expect bright cherry, dried herbs, earthy notes, and that signature tangy acidity. Approachable and food-friendly.

*Chianti Classico Riserva*
A step up in quality and aging. Must be aged a minimum of 24 months (at least 3 months in bottle). The extra time in oak adds more complexity — think dried cherry, leather, tobacco, spice, and a more structured tannic backbone. Generally richer and more age-worthy than the standard Classico.

*Chianti Classico Gran Selezione* (bonus tier!)
The top of the pyramid — single vineyard or best-barrel selection, aged 30+ months. The most concentrated and cellar-worthy of the three.

*In short:* Riserva = more oak, more age, more complexity, higher price point. For a casual dinner, Classico is fantastic. For a special occasion or a big steak, Riserva is worth the upgrade.

Want me to pull up some options from either tier?
